question.text: A Cat III manager expecting a market correction would MOST LIKELY position which strategy type?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Short-bias maintains net-short exposure — benefits from downward moves. Dedicated-long bleeds in corrections. Pre-IPO and Activist are long-oriented. **The Trap:** Others have net-long posture. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C same. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Short-bias funds should communicate expected performance in a 3-month rolling window, NOT monthly — shorts often bleed time value in choppy markets before big falls. Monthly comparisons to NIFTY cause investor churn at the worst time.
